summary: Agenzia delle Entrate page (last updated 7 March 2025) explaining the codice fiscale: a 16-character code that identifies people in dealings with public bodies. It says that for foreign citizens who apply for or renew a permesso di soggiorno, the Questura assigns the code; residents abroad can ask an Italian consulate. People without a code can request one with form AA4/8 by PEC or at any Agenzia office by appointment; a non-EU applicant attaches a valid passport with visa, a valid permesso, or another listed ID. A first code for a foreign citizen needs an in-person appointment for identification. A certificate of assignment is issued while the Tessera Sanitaria or code card is pending.

Agenzia delle Entrate information sheet (last updated 30 October 2023). To open, change, or close a partita IVA for a professional activity or other activity that does not require registration in the Registro delle imprese or the REA, an individual fills in and sends form AA9/12 to the Agenzia. For a business or craft activity, it says to use the Comunicazione Unica d'impresa (an Infocamere service), which also handles registration in the Registro delle imprese or REA. The page does not mention visas or digital nomads.

Agenzia delle Entrate page on how to open a partita IVA for a professional activity not requiring Registro delle imprese registration. Form AA9/12 is filed within 30 days of the start of the activity: by PEC (subject 'Dichiarazione di inizio attività', with ID copy if signed by hand), in person or by delegate at any Agenzia office by appointment, or by registered mail with an ID copy. It adds a special rule for non-EU/EEA residents who appoint a tax representative (filing only at that representative's provincial office, with set declarations and guarantees), and says the form can be prepared with Agenzia software and sent online from the reserved area. The page does not mention visas or digital nomads.

Gazzetta Ufficiale text of the interministerial decree of 29 February 2024 (Interior, Foreign Affairs, Tourism, Labour), preamble and Art. 1. Art. 1 says the decree sets how to enter and get a permesso di soggiorno, which highly qualified workers can benefit, the minimum income limits, and how the work is verified. It applies to non-EU citizens doing highly qualified work remotely with technology, either self-employed or for a company that may be outside Italy. Entry and stay over 90 days is allowed outside the annual quotas, without prejudice to art. 27-quater and 27-quinquies routes; for stays under 90 days the visa and permesso under Arts. 3 and 4 are still needed.

Art. 2 of the 29 February 2024 decree (definitions). A 'digital nomad' is a foreigner doing self-employed work (lavoro autonomo) remotely through technology. A 'remote worker' is a foreigner doing subordinate (employee) work or collaboration remotely, under art. 2(1) of D.Lgs. 81/2015. 'Highly qualified work' means work by someone meeting art. 27-quater(1) of D.Lgs. 286/1998. A 'company, even if not resident in Italy' is an employer or client that professionally runs an organised economic activity and may have its registered office outside Italy. A third-country national is anyone who is not an EU citizen.

Art. 3 of the 29 February 2024 decree (requirements for the visa and permesso). Workers must: have minimum annual income from lawful sources not below three times the minimum level for exemption from healthcare cost-sharing (no euro figure); health insurance for medical care and hospital stays valid in Italy for the stay; suitable documentation on housing; at least six months' prior experience in the work; and, for remote workers, the work or collaboration contract or binding offer for work needing an art. 27-quater qualification. No provisional nulla osta (nomads) or work nulla osta (remote workers) is needed. The visa is refused or revoked if an employer resident in Italy has listed convictions in the last five years; the applicant files the employer's signed declaration with ID.

Art. 4 of the 29 February 2024 decree (permesso di soggiorno). The holder of the visa must request the permesso directly at the Questura of the province where they are, within eight working days of entry. It reads 'nomade digitale - lavoratore da remoto', lasts no more than one year, and is renewable yearly if the conditions remain. The holder shows the visa documents stamped by the consulate. It is refused or revoked if requirements lapse, if tax and contribution rules are not respected, or if the employer has listed convictions. Family reunification is allowed for the relatives in art. 29(1)(a) and (b) of the Testo unico, under the conditions of art. 29; they get a family permesso of the same length as the worker's. The Questura sends the contract to the labour inspectorate.

Art. 6 of the 29 February 2024 decree (tax compliance). For digital nomads and remote workers, the Questura generates and communicates the codice fiscale when it issues the permesso. Digital nomads must also request a partita IVA under art. 35 of DPR 633/1972; no deadline is set in this article and remote workers are not mentioned for it. The Questura notifies the Agenzia delle Entrate of the permesso electronically. Ordinary tax-audit rules apply, and the Agenzia informs the Questura if tax violations are found.

Prefettura di Roma page (last updated 21 May 2024) on registering at the anagrafe. An adult family member registers in person at the Comune where they live, also declaring minor children. Needed: a permesso valid over 3 months, a valid passport, the codice fiscale, and civil-status papers not shown in the passport (birth, marriage, etc.), translated and legalised. Registration is completed after local police confirm you live at the address. Registration is needed for things like a driving licence and the national health service. Other points: data must match across passport and permesso; renew the residence declaration within 60 days of renewing the permesso; moving Comune is filed within 20 days; how to get an identity card.

Foreign Ministry 'Il visto per l'Italia' page for the long-stay (type D) visa type 'Missione' (code 13_0_D), under 'rights and duties for stays over 90 days'. For mission entries it says the permesso request is sent through authorised post offices (Sportello Amico) with a kit; patronati and Comuni help for free; the post office gives a receipt with login codes for the Portale Immigrazione and the fingerprint appointment; the Questura later calls the applicant to collect the permesso. General warnings: non-EU citizens with a regular permesso must register at the anagrafe of their Comune; the integration agreement for permits of at least one year; health cover rules by purpose of stay. It has no digital-nomad section.

summary: Foreign Ministry 'Il visto per l'Italia' home page. It offers a four-question guided check (nationality, country of residence, length of stay, purpose) to tell whether a visa is needed and which forms apply. It says the information is only indicative and not exhaustive, that applicants should contact the Italian mission for their place of residence, that submitting documents does not necessarily mean a visa is issued, and that border authorities may ask again for proof of the visa requirements. It also notes the EU Entry/Exit System (EES) from 12 October 2025 for short stays. The purpose list shown does not include a digital-nomad option.

summary: Normattiva text of art. 27-quater D.Lgs. 286/1998 (in force from 18 Dec 2025), on highly qualified workers and the EU Blue Card. Comma 1 lists the alternative qualifications: a tertiary degree of at least three years or a post-secondary qualification of at least three years or EQF/QNQ level 6; the requirements of D.Lgs. 206/2007 for regulated professions; a higher professional qualification shown by at least five years of comparable experience; or, for ICT managers and specialists (ISCO-08 133 and 25), at least three years of relevant experience in the seven years before applying. The rest covers the Blue Card procedure, refusals, and Blue Card family reunification.

summary: Normattiva text of art. 29 D.Lgs. 286/1998 (family reunification). Comma 1 lists who can be reunited: (a) a spouse not legally separated and at least 18; (b) minor children, including the spouse's or those born outside marriage, unmarried, with the other parent's consent; (c) adult dependent children with total disability; (d) dependent parents under set conditions. Comma 3: the sponsor must show housing meeting the Comune's suitability checks and lawful annual income of at least the assegno sociale plus half of it per family member (no euro figure printed). Comma 7: the nulla osta request, with those documents, goes online to the prefettura's Sportello unico; the consulate checks that kinship documents are authentic. Comma 8: nulla osta within 150 days.
notes_for_cap: Read 2026-10-16 by curl (HTTP 200). Note: art. 4.6 of the 2024 decree only extends letters a) and b) to nomads/remote workers.

summary: Normattiva text of art. 4 D.Lgs. 286/1998 (entry into Italy). Entry needs a valid passport or equivalent travel document and a valid visa, travel authorisation, or permesso, under Schengen rules, through official border crossings. Visas are issued by Italian missions in the country of origin or stable residence. Comma 3: the foreigner must show documents confirming purpose and conditions of stay and sufficient means; entry is refused to those seen as a threat to public order or security or convicted of listed offences. Comma 4-bis: national-visa applicants give biometric identifiers, subject to exemptions set by ministerial decree. False documents make the application inadmissible. It also covers EES and ETIAS.

summary: Polizia di Stato page (24 Jun 2014, modified 5 Jan 2024) on issuing the permesso di soggiorno. First arrivals have 8 working days to request it from the Questore of the province where they intend to stay, in some cases via authorised post offices. Issue and renewal take on average 60 days. You bring the request form, passport with visa and a copy, 4 identical photos, documents for the permit type, and the fee. Contribution: €40 for permits over three months up to one year, €50 over one to two years, €100 for some others; minors are exempt. A minor child gets an individual electronic permit. Permits of at least one year require an integration agreement. It does not mention the digital-nomad permit specifically.

summary: Boston consulate page for the digital nomad / remote worker visa. Two categories (nomads: freelancers; remote workers: employees), work meeting art. 27-quater. Documents include: passport valid 15 months past travel with two blank pages; proof of residence in the jurisdiction; visa form and photo; travel medical insurance of at least €30,000 or $50,000; proof of qualifying profession; a lease, rental contract, or deed in the applicant's name for the whole visa (hotel or hospitality not accepted); income of at least three times the healthcare-exemption minimum, printed as €24,789 'at the time of this writing in 2024', from the work, not passive income; six months' experience. Remote workers add a contract and employer no-convictions letter. No police certificate is listed.

New York consulate general visa information. Appointments are online only via Prenot@Mi, free, and must be confirmed 3 to 10 days before; a waiting list exists; you can book at most 180 days before departure; applicants appear in person. Only residents of the listed jurisdiction (NY, CT, certain NJ counties, Bermuda) may apply, with proof such as a driver's license. Non-US citizens show US legal residence. Passport valid 3 months beyond the trip with two visa pages. Processing generally varies from 7 days to several weeks. Fees by money order or certified check; they change every 3 months. Originals plus copies; passports returned by USPS prepaid envelope only. Minors need a birth certificate, notarized parental consent, and both parents present.

Washington Embassy page on booking visa appointments (last updated 9 June 2026). Elective-residence and digital nomad / remote worker applicants must email visti.washington@esteri.it before booking. In general, appointments are booked on Prenot@Mi, up to 6 months in advance and no later than 15 days before the intended departure. The office may cancel appointments booked by residents of other consular jurisdictions. On confirmation it says verbatim: 'You must remember to CONFIRM your appointment at least 10 days before, but NO LATER than 3 days from your scheduled departure date, through the Prenot@Mi website.' The page leaves the window ambiguous. If cancelled, a new appointment must be booked, which may delay departure.
